DECISIONS:
Q1: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: B fixes the actual hole without needing new access. The squash auto-merge at `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2031` is pinned with `--match-head-commit`, but the README says GitHub can keep an enabled auto-merge across later pushes while checks are pending. So a new head can merge before its own review finishes. Turning auto-merge off on `synchronize` (A) stops that for normal pushes. A status check tied to the head SHA also stops it for pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which fire no `synchronize` event and so slip past A. C is rejected for three reasons: it needs an admin-scoped token, it changes branch protection in consumer repos without review, and the setting it automates is a one-time repo choice that doesn't need to run on a schedule. The code for turning off auto-merge already exists in `scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh`, where the judge withdraws auto-merge when blocking findings remain. That path should be extended rather than written a second time.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1: (letter decision; these notes tell the planner where B goes in the code)
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (gate job; the auto-merge steps around lines 2013 and 2031)
    - scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh (existing helper that turns off auto-merge)
    - scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh (security-pass gate, outcomes clean/hold/…)
    - scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh (`REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS`, used if a new helper script is added)
  steps:
    - On `pull_request.synchronize`, the gate turns off any enabled auto-merge on the PR. It reuses or moves out the existing helper, uses the `GH_PAT` the gate already holds, and logs a stable prefix with an outcome (for example disabled, not_enabled or failed). If the API call fails, the run fails closed: it does not merge, and the review run that follows decides.
    - When the gate sees a new head, it posts a commit status with the fixed context `ai-review/head-gate` and state `pending` on that SHA.
    - It sets `success` on that same SHA only when review/autofix has passed and the single-issue security pass is clean (or legitimately skipped or disabled) for exactly that SHA. It does this just before or with the head-bound `gh pr merge --match-head-commit` call. Hold, failed and stale outcomes leave the status at pending, or set failure.
    - The deterministic-skip merge path and the review-blocked judge merge path set the same status, bound to the head SHA they evaluated.
    - Any new variable (for example an enable switch or the context name) gets a default inside the helper script.
    - Add contract tests that pin these behaviours: auto-merge is turned off on synchronize, the status context name is fixed, success is posted only after the gates pass for the matching SHA, and a failure to turn off auto-merge fails closed.
    - Update README, agents.md and a `changelog.d/` fragment with how to add `ai-review/head-gate` as a required check in branch protection. Nothing changes branch protection automatically.
    - Check the size of `review_autofix.yml` with `wc -c` against the 480,000-byte guard. If it is over, move the large new step bodies into `scripts/review_autofix_step_<slug>.sh`.
  reversibility: Turning off auto-merge on synchronize can't strand a PR, because the next review turns it back on for a head that passes. The status has no effect until a repo makes it required, and an enable switch with a default can turn the feature off.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- None: no new credentials are needed. Posting statuses and turning off auto-merge use the `GH_PAT` the gate already holds (repo scope). Repos that want the status enforced must add `ai-review/head-gate` as a required check in their own branch protection. Until they do, the status is advisory only and turning off auto-merge on `synchronize` is the only protection.
